Live from NPR News in Washington, D.C., I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump continued his campaign blitz across the country Sunday.
As member station WDET's Quinn Kleinfelder reports, Trump held a rally before a crowd
of thousands in the battleground state of Michigan.
Trump spent much of his speech blasting Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, calling
his progressive policies, and attempted a socialist takeover of the nation.
The president barely touched on issues like the high cost of living, tariffs, or the war
in Iran.
Trump did argue increased fuel prices are only a short-term dilemma.
Are you kidding?
I thought gas would be double and triple, and it's a small price to pay for taking a
nuclear weapon away from maniacs.
The rally was on the border with Canada, which Trump claims is "willing to give us anything"
to end the current trade war.
For NPR News, I'm Quinn Kleinfelder in Detroit.
It's still not clear why Ukraine's access to Starlink Internet service was curtailed
last week.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk blames Ukraine for misusing the service, but Ukraine denies that.
Democratic Senator Adam Schiff says it's time to find out just what happened.
Defense Secretary Hegsetz should be brought in.
Anyone who has knowledge of what happened, you've got the president saying one thing,
you've got Elon Musk saying another thing.
You have them both saying different things at different times.
Somebody is lying here.
Maybe they're all lying in different ways, but we need to find out.
Schiff was speaking Sunday on NBC's Meet the Press.
The U.S. is dealing with the worst measles resurgence in decades, with cases particularly
high in Pennsylvania.
NPR's Shondali Stuster has more.
Pennsylvania officials are urging residents to get fully vaccinated against measles amid
new cases across the state.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health says over 1,300 cases of measles have been confirmed
in 44 counties across the state so far this year.
There were at least 21 new measles cases as of last week.
More than 250 people have been hospitalized and 5 people have died from measles in Pennsylvania.
Across the U.S., there have been more than 4,500 measles cases so far, which is more
than double the number of cases last year.
The CDC says that the vaccination status of 96 percent of those who have contracted measles
this year is "unvaccinated or unknown."
Shondali Stuster, NPR News.
Incumbent Brazilian President Luis Inacío Lula da Silva has won Sunday's presidential
election there.
With more than 95 percent of the vote counted, he holds a lead of more than 4 million votes.
It was a comeback win for Lula, who lost to challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in a first round
of voting just earlier this month.
Bolsonaro so far refused to concede his loss.
Shares in Asia are falling after a retreat last week on Wall Street, but U.S. futures
are up slightly.
You're listening to NPR News.
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado has returned
to Venezuela.
She had been in exile for the last 10 months.
She made her first public appearance Sunday at a church in the western part of the country.
With U.K. power-gritted increased danger from extreme weather and cyberattack, British retailers
are reporting a big boom in the sale of a formerly niche item, wind-up radios, Vicky
Barker reports from London.
Just days after the British government put them on its list of emergency supplies that
Brits should be stockpiling, wind-up radios are flying off the shelves.
At Ranger Army Surplus in Greater London, merchant Pav was left scratching his head,
telling the BBC.
They've just been sitting there on the shelves for a long time with not much attention.
And all of a sudden, out of nowhere, just all of them sold out.
Well, not quite out of nowhere.
The government warned that battery-operated or wind-up FM radios could be the only way
Brits can remain informed in the event of a local or national emergency.
For NPR News, I'm Vicky Barker in London.
The DC Studios horror movie Clayface landed in first place this weekend, bringing in $24
million in ticket sales from North American theaters.
The documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, You Can See Everything, was in second, adding
$19.5 million.
In two weeks, it's brought in $45.1 million, making it one of the highest-grossing documentaries
ever.
And the stop-motion animation movie Wildwood finished in third place, bringing in $11.8
million in ticket sales.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
